text.title: Rust Ownership Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes 3-question answers to a canonical parameter kind, then walks the crate-level audit gates. Leaves reference rules from 01-core-rules.xml; the skip leaf is always reachable.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the function keep the value after returning (store / return / drop later)?

branch.when: scope == throwaway_script OR scope == proc_macro OR scope == ffi_wrapper OR scope == generated_code OR scope == embedded_no_heap

conclusion.verdict: SKIP — signature-first ownership fights the ecosystem here

branch.question: Does another scope also keep the value?
Do the holders live in different threads?

conclusion.verdict: `Rc<T>` (single-threaded ref count). RefCell only if genuine graph cycle.

branch.question: Does the function modify the value?

section.title: Crate-level audit gates
section.p: Walked once per crate, not once per signature — this is what the CI script checks.

decision-tree.root-question: What does the crate-wide audit surface?

conclusion.verdict: BLOCK — replace with Arc<Mutex> / Arc<RwLock> at the boundary
BLOCK — re-audit the signature; borrow or lift the value instead
BLOCK — split the scope so the borrows do not overlap
BLOCK — move the value instead of copying it
BLOCK — write the lifetime and name what outlives what
APPROVE — record the clone baseline and gate regressions on it

text.example: keeps_value=false (function reads file, returns parsed struct, drops input path) → modifies=false → `&Path` parameter. Compare to `fn load(path: PathBuf)` antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml str-vs-string-confusion.
